title: Library pathways
note: Page copy for docs/program/library-pathways/index.html and docs/program/LIBRARY-PATHWAYS-2026-11.md. Tokens: {{c:key}} is a count computed from the data files (tag M); {{n:value|TAG}} is a literal number with its tag. Edit here and rebuild with build-page.js.txt.

policy_says.top_first: Opus does the work. If the gate catches a wrong answer, Fable tries. No library.
policy_says.cheap_ladder: The cheap model tries first. A caught failure gets one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable. No library.
policy_says.library: The same ladder, plus the library: a lookup before the cheap attempt, and Opus or Fable solves written back as entries.

hero: A working model of the library design. A piece of work enters at the left and passes the design's steps. Each line is a way it can go. The thicker the line, the more work goes that way under the current settings.
There are no fixes on this page, and no judgment on whether the library reaches its goal. The page shows what the model gives under stated assumptions.

tags.M: Measured on this PC, in the owner's repositories or session records.
tags.S: Taken from an outside study or the vendor's price list.

computed_tag: A number the model computes takes the weakest tag of its inputs. Every computed number here uses at least one guess, so it is tagged G. In a table or tree, the tag at the top applies to every number below it.
words: Piece of work
One fix-sized task of about ten cheap calls, where a result is made and checked. The model files call it an episode.
Visible or latent
Visible: something signals a problem (an error, a failing check, a stated bug). Latent: nothing signals that a choice matters.
Entry
One stored conclusion in the library.
Look-alike
A stored entry that looks like a match but has a different cause.
Gate
Whatever decides a result is right: tests, and sometimes a review by Opus.
Ladder
What happens after a caught failure: one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable.
Tier
A model level on the ladder: the cheap model (Sonnet), Opus, Fable.
Cost
Counted in cheap-call equivalents. One cheap-model call costs one. An Opus call costs the Opus price ratio.
Wrong rate
The share of pieces of work that do not end accepted and right: escaped (found later or never) or caught and never solved.
Stock
Something that piles up over time, drawn as a box. Here: good entries and bad entries.
Flow
What fills or drains a stock each period, drawn as a thick arrow with a valve.
Loop R or B
A chain of causes that returns to where it started. R (reinforcing) feeds itself. B (balancing) holds itself back.

map.title: The map
map.lede: Pick one piece of work and a way of working. The graph shows where that piece can go. The tree under it lists every route, heaviest first. Tap a route to light it up on the graph, then step through it.
map.graph_note: Boxes are states. Lines are branches. Line weight is the share of this piece of work that takes the branch. A dashed hairline carries nothing under these settings. Top band: the model's stages. Under each stage: which of the design's ten steps it stands for.
map.tree_note: Every route from start to outcome for this piece of work. Branches shared by several routes are drawn once. Heaviest first.

cases.title: Where real cases broke
cases.lede: {{c:cases}} real cases from the owner's two repositories and session records were walked through the design's ten steps. Each cell is one step of one case.
cases.warning: These are chosen problem cases. They show where the design breaks. They do not show how often.
cases.judged: Each status is the judgment of the agent that walked the case, from the records. Tap a row to read the case.

lims.title: The limitations, placed on the map
lims.lede: {{c:lims}} limitations came out of the walks and two thought-experiment lists. Each sits at the design step where it acts. Tap one to see its steps and branches on the map.
lims.map_note: Shaded stages: the steps the limitation touches; the darker band is its main step. Heavy lines: the branches whose chance or cost uses one of its unknowns.
lims.works_lede: Places where the design worked, or would have helped, in a real case. They come from the same walks.

run.title: Run it
run.lede: Every unknown in the model has a slider. Move one and the whole page follows: the map, the routes, the outputs and the stock drawing.
run.outputs_note: Cost per piece of work, in cheap-call equivalents. Wrong rate: the share of pieces of work that do not end accepted and right.
run.two_comparisons: Two comparisons, always together. Against the cheap model with the ladder: what the library itself adds. Against the strong model directly: the owner's goal, which also depends on the ladder and the gate.
run.ratio_read: A ratio is the library's figure divided by the other way's figure. Below one: the library's figure is lower. Above one: it is higher.

many.title: Many runs
many.lede: Most unknowns are guesses. So the model is run many times. Each run draws every unknown at random, evenly, from its range. The result is a spread, not one answer.
many.follows: This spread follows from the assumed ranges. Change a range and it changes. It is not a measurement of the library.
many.rank_read: How strongly each ratio rises (+) or falls (-) as one unknown rises across the runs. One means it always moves with it; zero means no steady link. The measure is the rank correlation.

leaves.title: What the map leaves out
leaves.lede: The model's own limits, in plain words. They come from the model brief and from the independent check of the engine.

loops.name: Bad entries bring more bad entries
loops.text: More bad entries raise the share of bad entries a lookup returns. More wrong entries reach the cheap attempt and spoil work. More work climbs to Opus or Fable. More strong-tier solves and escapes get written, some of them bad.

loops.name: More entries, more look-alikes
loops.text: Every entry, good or bad, raises the chance a misleading look-alike can be retrieved. Accepted look-alikes spoil work, more work climbs the ladder, and more entries get written.

loops.name: Good entries thin their own supply
loops.text: More good entries fill the library. The cheap model is right more often with an entry in hand, so less work climbs to Opus or Fable, and fewer new entries are written.

loops.name: Good entries go stale
loops.text: Each period a share of the good entries goes stale and moves to the bad stock. The more good entries there are, the more go stale.

design_steps_note: The walkthroughs used the design's ten steps. The model splits the work into eleven stages and an outcome. This match between them was set by hand: step 1 (what is in the window) has no stage of its own and is shown with the trigger; step 6 (use) covers the screen and the cheap attempt.

leaves_out.t: A model of the mechanism, not a forecast
leaves_out.x: Its numbers follow from its settings. {{c:guess}} of the {{c:drawn}} unknowns that are drawn are guesses.

leaves_out.t: Chosen cases, not a sample of work
leaves_out.x: The {{c:cases}} cases were chosen because something went wrong. They show which routes exist and where steps break. They never show how often.
Works, strains and breaks were set by the agents that walked the cases from the records. Another reader could set some differently.
Every piece of work is treated as about ten cheap calls. Real work varies far more in size, and a large piece is not the same as many small ones.

leaves_out.t: Calls are the same size inside a tier
leaves_out.x: The cost unit is one cheap-model call. The price ratios are per token, so they equal the per-call ratio only if calls are the same size in every tier. On this PC's records an Opus call averaged {{n:about 222,000|M}} cache-read tokens and a Sonnet call {{n:about 440,000|M}}. On that data the per-call ratio would be near one, while the model fixes it at two.

leaves_out.t: Time and attention are not counted
leaves_out.x: Tests at the gate cost nothing. Waiting, wall-clock time and the owner's attention are left out. A lookup counts as calls; a mechanical check, carrying an entry and a handoff cost cheap-call equivalents but count as no calls.

A piece's kind, what the cheap model would do, what the library holds and whether a look-alike exists are combined by multiplying their chances. Real work clusters: a hard problem may also be the one the library lacks.

The two stocks change by their expected amounts each period. A real library has one history, with luck in it. Each period is worked out on the stocks at its start, and staleness acts on those starting stocks.
A good entry is good wherever it applies, and a bad one bad. Partly right shows up only as the composite 'some parts' result.
Projects are not separated. Facts that differ between projects act only through the look-alike and wrong-entry chances.
A wrong accepted entry acts only at the cheap attempt. It does not follow the work up the ladder.

leaves_out.t: A fixed ladder and one gate
leaves_out.x: One cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable, in that order. Real sessions skip rungs, repeat them, or end with the owner. The chance the gate catches a wrong output does not depend on which model made it.
A bad entry turns good only when a found escape is repaired. Staleness moves good entries to bad, never the other way.
The number of periods is a chosen horizon, never drawn. The Opus price ratio has a range of one value, so the runs never vary it.

leaves_out.t: Ranges are drawn evenly and on their own
leaves_out.x: If two unknowns move together in reality, the runs do not know it. The ranking measures steady rise or fall inside the ranges. It misses an effect that rises and then falls.

leaves_out.t: Some limitations act through nothing here
leaves_out.x: {{c:noparam}} limitations name no unknown, so the model cannot show them: {{c:noparam_ids}}.

Several figures tagged M or S were measured on a different unit than the setting they stand for; each slider's source says how. One outside figure supports two settings in a row: the chance a wrong entry is accepted, and the chance it then spoils the work.
If a draw makes 'all parts' plus 'some parts' exceed certainty, both are scaled down in proportion; the three ceilings on what the library can hold likewise. With the current ranges neither happens.

leaves_out.t: The step match is drawn by hand
leaves_out.x: The walkthroughs' ten steps and the model's stages are matched by a table, shown on the map. A limitation is placed on the map through that table and through its unknowns.

layout.note: Positions of the states on the map: [column, row]. Branches between neighbouring columns are drawn as curves; longer ones run along a lane row (given here, else the target's row).
